source_document: LHDN official website table — Tahun Taksiran 2025 (Jenis Potongan Individu), cross-verified against Navigasi HASiL 2026 leaflet (updated 28/04/2026) and independent tax guide sources

data_quality_flags.issue: RESOLVED per user-confirmed LHDN e-Filing (MyTax/ezHasil) behavior: items 6, 7, and 8 are NOT independent categories. They share a single combined umbrella cap of RM10,000 (heading: 'Perbelanjaan perubatan bagi diri sendiri, suami/isteri atau anak'). Within that umbrella, item 7 is individually capped at RM1,000 and item 8 at RM6,000 by the e-Filing form itself; item 6 has no additional individual cap beyond its own internal vaccination/dental sub-caps. If the sum of all three exceeds RM10,000, the system restricts total claimable relief to RM10,000. Schema restructured below to reflect this: a new medical_combined_umbrella parent (RM10,000) with items 6, 7, and 8 all as its children, each still carrying their own individual limit_amount as an additional constraint layered under the shared umbrella.

engine_note: For categories with a shared umbrella cap (sub_cap_parent_id pointing to a parent that itself has multiple direct children, e.g. medical_combined_umbrella), the relief calculation engine must apply BOTH constraints: (1) each child's own limit_amount individually, AND (2) the sum of all children's claimed amounts capped at the parent's limit_amount. This differs from a simple single sub-cap (e.g. medical_vaccination_subcap under medical_serious_vaccination_dental), which only needs its own limit checked since it's the only sub-cap consuming that parent's headroom in this dataset. FR-4.2 (parent-child limit logic) should be built to handle the general case: sum of children vs parent ceiling, not just single-child sub-caps.
